+# Typed decision-model post-training
+
+These notebooks use framework-owned CLM/CLEF/D1 APIs with a newly authored fictional fixture. They cover released baselines, head adaptation, supervised training, optional policy continuation, validation selection, checkpoint persistence and heldout reporting. No training results, model weights or executed outputs are bundled. The small fixture checks mechanics; it is not a security benchmark.
+
+| Notebook | Workflow |
+| --- | --- |
+| [00 Fictional data](00_fictional_data.ipynb) | Deterministic typed questions, exact policy labels, per-option utilities and split hashes |
+| [01 CLM supervised and utility](01_clm_supervised_and_utility.ipynb) | Frozen encoder, released head baseline, supervised heads, optional exact expected utility or sampled GRPO |
+| [02 CLEF heads or LoRA](02_clef_heads_or_lora.ipynb) | Frozen schema head or backbone LoRA plus schema head; optional utility continuation and local merged export |
+| [03 CLM contrastive heads](03_clm_contrastive_heads.ipynb) | Bidirectional InfoNCE on cached frozen features, with repeated-positive false-negative masking |
+| [04 D1 readouts](04_d1_readouts.ipynb) | Frozen D1-3B answer-token rows or D1 Omni marker head; baseline, SFT and optional utility continuation |
+| [05 Optional Data Designer](05_optional_data_designer.ipynb) | Public-provider writer/judge paraphrases, source-case split assignment, identifier filtering and frozen new manifests |
+| [06 Experimental calibration continuation](06_experimental_calibration_continuation.ipynb) | Gaussian logit proposals, correctness/confidence reward, group baseline and CE anchor; validation Brier selection |
+
+Paired `.py` files contain the same workflow in percent-cell format. Default `RUN_TRAINING=False` and `RUN_GENERATION=False` create fresh local fixture files and display planned commands. They do not launch subprocesses, load models or call services. Run notebooks from this repository or their tutorial directory so repository discovery succeeds. Generated runs use new timestamped directories under ignored `runs/`; existing datasets are never replaced.
+
+## CPU preview and fixture checks
+
+From the repository root, use an isolated CPU interpreter; these helpers require only the standard library:
+
+```bash
+PYTHONPATH=tutorials/decision_models uv run --no-project python -m unittest discover   -s tutorials/decision_models -p 'test_tutorial_contracts.py' -v
+PYTHONPATH=tutorials/decision_models uv run --no-project python -m decision_tutorial.data   --output-dir tutorials/decision_models/runs/my-fixture --seed 7
+uv run --no-project --with jupyterlab --with matplotlib jupyter lab tutorials/decision_models
+```
+
+The checked-in `fixtures/smoke/` has 16 train, 8 validation and 8 test records, each with five questions. Training notebooks generate 128/32/32 records. Identifiers use `.example`, `example.com` and RFC 5737 IP addresses. Exact state content and IDs are disjoint across splits; scenario templates intentionally repeat. Gold answers stay outside the model-visible `state`. This policy and all fixture records were authored for this tutorial without copying an operational corpus.
+
+## Enable a model experiment
+
+Prepare the framework's supported Linux GPU environment using its [installation instructions](../../README.md), then use that environment as the notebook kernel. CLM loads a public Qwen3-8B encoder; CLEF loads a 27B backbone even for head-only training. Choose `NPROC` and, where exposed, `TP` for your allocated hardware. Head-only training freezes backbone gradients but still needs memory for forward passes. Download access and model license requirements remain those of the selected publisher. Optional learning curves need `matplotlib` in the kernel environment.
+
+Set `RUN_TRAINING=True` only when ready to run the displayed native commands. CLM caches the baseline's frozen embeddings, then reuses them across stages. CLEF `HEAD_ONLY=True` is the default; `False` enables LoRA plus the joint head. Keep this choice consistent across checkpoint reloads. Saved heads/adapters remain in the run directory. CLEF merged export is an explicit optional action for LoRA stages and may require substantial disk and memory.
+
+`ENABLE_UTILITY=True` continues the selected SFT stage. Exact expected utility is the default because every candidate utility is known. Native sampled GRPO is also available: select `UTILITY_OBJECTIVE="grpo"` in notebooks 01/02 and inspect the recipe's group size, temperature, KL and supervised-anchor settings. This is an experimental configuration choice rather than a claim that sampling is superior. Notebook 06 demonstrates a separate experimental calibration-aware objective inspired by the [JevAny recipe](https://github.com/SimpleJev/JevAny/blob/main/recipes/rlcr.toml); it does not reproduce a proprietary training method or guarantee gains.
+
+## Interpret a run
+
+Use training data for fitting, validation for checkpoint selection and test only for final reporting. Baseline/SFT/continuation stages use the same generated split paths. Retain `data/manifest.json` and verify its hashes when comparing runs. The CSV helper checks common record/decision counts; equal counts do not prove identical heldout records. Preserve model revisions, trainable scope, topology, seed and recipe values with your results. Repeat training seeds before making effectiveness claims.
+
+Native reports retain decision accuracy, exact record match, NLL, Brier, calibration summaries, utility and metadata slices. A utility gain can accompany worse accuracy or probability quality. The notebooks plot actual local objective and validation observations; they make no fixed improvement claim. Objective logs may be per-update/main-rank observations and do not equal a full training-set loss. Checkpoint self-reload, publisher agreement and cross-framework numerical equivalence require separate tests.
+
+## Optional generated prose
+
+Notebook 05 needs `uv pip install data-designer==0.9.4 pandas pyarrow` in the chosen environment and your own `NVIDIA_API_KEY` only when generation is enabled. Inspect its two-record preview before `REVIEWED_PREVIEW=True`. Labels and utility tables remain policy-derived; writer/judge output changes only observation prose. Source cases keep their original split and appear at most once. Automated checks do not prove factual accuracy or absence of personal data; inspect generated text before sharing it. Generated data defines a new experiment and must not replace an existing split silently.
+
+## Experimental D1 readouts
+
+[04 D1 readouts](04_d1_readouts.ipynb) covers D1-3B additive answer-token rows and the D1 Omni marker head through native framework models. It keeps the backbone frozen, selects readouts on validation, and reports baseline/SFT/optional utility stages on the same heldout split. Use a prepared single-GPU environment; this source preparation did not run D1 GPU training, publisher comparisons or media paths. The fictional observations are text-only and establish no image/audio adaptation result or numerical-parity claim. The implementation follows the repository's Apache 2.0 license; downloaded publisher weights and remote components retain their [publisher license](https://www.liquid.ai/lfm-license).
+
+The tutorial code and newly authored fixture follow this repository's [Apache 2.0 license](../../LICENSE). Downloaded models, publisher runtime components and third-party packages retain their own licenses. Model weights are not bundled in these tutorials. This source preparation has CPU checks only; no new GPU training, API generation or model export is claimed.
+

CLM obtains frozen Qwen3-8B embeddings through AutoBridge's existing backbone provider; CLEF uses its existing backbone provider plus the joint schema head. +"""Deterministic, fictional typed-decision data for tutorial smoke tests."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import ipaddress
+import json
+import logging
+import random
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Literal, TypedDict
+
+
+LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class Question(TypedDict):
+    """A question in the public typed-decision request format."""
+
+    type: Literal["choice", "score", "noul"]
+    instructions: str
+    criteria: dict[str, str] | list[str]
+
+
+class Record(TypedDict):
+    """One fictional observation, gold decisions and complete option utilities."""
+
+    id: str
+    state: dict[str, object]
+    questions: dict[str, Question]
+    answers: dict[str, str]
+    rewards: dict[str, dict[str, float]]
+    meta: dict[str, str]
+
+
+QUESTIONS: dict[str, Question] = {
+    "verdict": {
+        "type": "choice",
+        "instructions": "What explains the observed security alert?",
+        "criteria": {
+            "malicious": "The evidence supports an unauthorized attack.",
+            "benign_authorized": "The activity is authorized and expected.",
+            "false_positive": "A sensor artifact explains the alert.",
+        },
+    },
+    "action": {
+        "type": "choice",
+        "instructions": "Which response follows the tutorial policy?",
+        "criteria": {
+            "close": "Close the alert.",
+            "monitor": "Monitor the asset without containment.",
+            "escalate": "Ask an analyst to investigate.",
+            "contain": "Contain the affected asset.",
+        },
+    },
+    "severity": {
+        "type": "score",
+        "instructions": "How severe is the event under the tutorial policy?",
+        "criteria": ["Informational", "Low", "Medium", "High", "Critical"],
+    },
+    "attack_tactic": {
+        "type": "choice",
+        "instructions": "Which behavior generated this alert?",
+        "criteria": {
+            "credential_access": "An attempt to obtain or misuse credentials.",
+            "execution": "A process or script execution event.",
+        },
+    },
+    "needs_human": {
+        "type": "noul",
+        "instructions": "Does the tutorial policy require analyst review?",
+        "criteria": {"false": "No analyst review is required.", "true": "An analyst must review the alert."},
+    },
+}
+
+
+def option_ids(question: Question) -> list[str]:
+    """Return semantic option IDs without imposing a model's native order."""
+    criteria = question["criteria"]
+    return [str(index) for index in range(len(criteria))] if isinstance(criteria, list) else list(criteria)
+
+
+def make_records(*, count: int, seed: int) -> list[Record]:
+    """Create new fictional records; identifiers use reserved example ranges."""
+    if count < 1:
+        raise ValueError("count must be positive")
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    records: list[Record] = []
+    for index in range(count):
+        verdict = rng.choice(["malicious", "benign_authorized", "false_positive"])
+        ambiguous = rng.choice([False, True])
+        critical = rng.choice([False, True])
+        tactic = rng.choice(["credential_access", "execution"])
+        explanations = {
+            "malicious": "A controlled test artifact matches the detection and no authorized change exists.",
+            "benign_authorized": "A signed maintenance ticket and the approved schedule explain the activity.",
+            "false_positive": "A replayed sensor event does not correspond to activity on this asset.",
+        }
+        action = "escalate" if ambiguous else ("contain" if verdict == "malicious" else "close")
+        severity = 3 + int(critical) if verdict == "malicious" else int(verdict == "benign_authorized")
+        answers = {
+            "verdict": verdict,
+            "action": action,
+            "severity": str(severity),
+            "attack_tactic": tactic,
+            "needs_human": "true" if ambiguous or (critical and verdict == "malicious") else "false",
+        }
+        rewards = {
+            name: {option: float(option == answers[name]) for option in option_ids(question)}
+            for name, question in QUESTIONS.items()
+        }
+        rewards["severity"] = {str(level): 1.0 - abs(level - severity) / 4 for level in range(5)}
+        if verdict == "malicious":
+            rewards["action"]["close"] = -1.0
+            rewards["verdict"]["benign_authorized"] = -1.0
+        address = f"192.0.2.{1 + index % 254}"
+        records.append(
+            {
+                "id": f"fictional-{seed}-{index:05d}",
+                "state": {
+                    "event_id": f"event-{seed}-{index:05d}",
+                    "asset": f"host-{index:05d}.example",
+                    "source_ip": address,
+                    "contact": f"analyst-{index:05d}@example.com",
+                    "behavior": "credential read attempt" if tactic == "credential_access" else "script execution",
+                    "evidence": explanations[verdict],
+                    "evidence_quality": "ambiguous" if ambiguous else "clear",
+                    "asset_impact": "critical" if critical else "ordinary",
+                },
+                "questions": json.loads(json.dumps(QUESTIONS)),
+                "answers": answers,
+                "rewards": rewards,
+                "meta": {"family": tactic, "verdict": verdict, "evidence": "ambiguous" if ambiguous else "clear"},
+            }
+        )
+    return records
+
+
+def validate_summary(summary: str) -> None:
+    """Reject obvious non-example identifiers in optional generated prose."""
+    for email in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.+%-]+@([A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", summary):
+        if email != "example.com" and not email.endswith(".example"):
+            raise ValueError("Generated prose contains a non-example email domain")
+    ranges = tuple(ipaddress.ip_network(net) for net in ("192.0.2.0/24", "198.51.100.0/24", "203.0.113.0/24"))
+    for value in re.findall(r"(?<![\w.])(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}(?![\w.])", summary):
+        address = ipaddress.ip_address(value)
+        if not any(address in network for network in ranges):
+            raise ValueError("Generated prose contains a non-documentation IP")
+    if re.search(r"-----BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY-----|\b(?:nvapi|sk)-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}", summary):
+        raise ValueError("Generated prose contains a credential-like string")
+
+
+def validate_splits(splits: dict[str, list[Record]]) -> None:
+    """Reject overlapping records, invalid targets and non-example identifiers."""
+    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
+    seen_states: set[str] = set()
+    documentation_range = ipaddress.ip_network("192.0.2.0/24")
+    for split, records in splits.items():
+        if not records:
+            raise ValueError(f"Empty split: {split}")
+        for record in records:
+            state = json.dumps(record["state"], sort_keys=True)
+            if record["id"] in seen_ids or state in seen_states:
+                raise ValueError(f"Repeated record or state: {record['id']}")
+            seen_ids.add(record["id"])
+            seen_states.add(state)
+            if record["questions"] != QUESTIONS:
+                raise ValueError("Question schema differs from the tutorial schema")
+            if ipaddress.ip_address(str(record["state"]["source_ip"])) not in documentation_range:
+                raise ValueError("source_ip must use the documentation range")
+            if not str(record["state"]["contact"]).endswith("@example.com"):
+                raise ValueError("contact must use example.com")
+            if not str(record["state"]["asset"]).endswith(".example"):
+                raise ValueError("asset must use the reserved .example suffix")
+            for name, question in QUESTIONS.items():
+                options = option_ids(question)
+                if record["answers"][name] not in options:
+                    raise ValueError(f"Unknown gold option for {name}")
+                if set(record["rewards"][name]) != set(options):
+                    raise ValueError(f"Utility options differ for {name}")
+
+
+def write_dataset(
+    output_dir: Path, *, train_records: int = 128, validation_records: int = 32, test_records: int = 32, seed: int = 7
+) -> dict[str, list[Record]]:
+    """Write a fresh dataset directory and a content-hash manifest.
+
+    Existing output directories are rejected so an experiment's splits cannot
+    be silently replaced. This fixture tests mechanics, not security efficacy.
+    """
+    if output_dir.exists():
+        raise FileExistsError(f"Choose a fresh dataset directory: {output_dir}")
+    counts = {"train": train_records, "validation": validation_records, "test": test_records}
+    if any(count < 1 for count in counts.values()):
+        raise ValueError("Every split must contain at least one record")
+    records = make_records(count=sum(counts.values()), seed=seed)
+    splits: dict[str, list[Record]] = {}
+    start = 0
+    for name, count in counts.items():
+        splits[name] = records[start : start + count]
+        start += count
+    validate_splits(splits)
+    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
+    hashes = {}
+    for name, part in splits.items():
+        path = output_dir / f"{name}.jsonl"
+        path.write_text("".join(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n" for record in part), encoding="utf-8")
+        hashes[name] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+    (output_dir / "questions.json").write_text(json.dumps(QUESTIONS, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    manifest = {"kind": "deterministic-fictional-smoke-data", "seed": seed, "counts": counts, "sha256": hashes}
+    (output_dir / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    return splits
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Generate fresh local smoke data without a network or model download."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=7)
+    parser.add_argument("--train-records", type=int, default=128)
+    parser.add_argument("--validation-records", type=int, default=32)
+    parser.add_argument("--test-records", type=int, default=32)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    splits = write_dataset(
+        args.output_dir,
+        train_records=args.train_records,
+        validation_records=args.validation_records,
+        test_records=args.test_records,
+        seed=args.seed,
+    )
+    LOGGER.info("Wrote %s", {name: len(records) for name, records in splits.items()})
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
+    main()

+"""Inspect locally generated framework reports without fixed performance claims."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import csv
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import TypedDict
+
+
+class StageResult(TypedDict):
+    """Held-out measurements for one stage of a local experiment."""
+
+    stage: str
+    records: int
+    decisions: int
+    accuracy: float
+    exact_match: float
+    nll: float
+    brier: float
+    reward: float
+
+
+def summarize_run(run_dir: Path, *, stages: tuple[str, ...] = ("base", "sft")) -> list[StageResult]:
+    """Read native test reports and require equal record and decision counts.
+
+    Equal counts do not establish record identity. Retain the same split manifest
+    and input files across stages; verify their hashes separately."""
+    rows: list[StageResult] = []
+    for stage in stages:
+        path = run_dir / stage / "metrics_test.json"
+        overall = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["overall"]
+        row: StageResult = {
+            "stage": stage,
+            "records": int(overall["records"]),
+            "decisions": int(overall["n"]),
+            **{key: float(overall[key]) for key in ("accuracy", "exact_match", "nll", "brier", "reward")},
+        }
+        if rows and (row["records"], row["decisions"]) != (rows[0]["records"], rows[0]["decisions"]):
+            raise ValueError("Stage reports have different record or decision counts")
+        rows.append(row)
+    return rows
+
+
+def write_summary(rows: list[StageResult], path: Path) -> None:
+    """Write a fresh CSV summary; accuracy and utility may move differently."""
+    if not rows:
+        raise ValueError("At least one stage is required")
+    with path.open("x", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
+        writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=list(StageResult.__annotations__))
+        writer.writeheader()
+        writer.writerows(rows)

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import hashlib
+import json
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from decision_tutorial.data import make_records, validate_splits, validate_summary, write_dataset
+from decision_tutorial.reporting import summarize_run
+
+
+class TutorialContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Test public fixture behavior without framework imports or downloads."""
+
+    def test_deterministic_disjoint_reserved_fixture(self) -> None:
+        """Identical seeds reproduce bytes and every split has distinct states."""
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp:
+            root = Path(temp)
+            first = write_dataset(root / "first", train_records=16, validation_records=8, test_records=8)
+            second = write_dataset(root / "second", train_records=16, validation_records=8, test_records=8)
+            self.assertEqual(first, second)
+            for name in first:
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    hashlib.sha256((root / "first" / f"{name}.jsonl").read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+                    hashlib.sha256((root / "second" / f"{name}.jsonl").read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+                )
+            self.assertEqual(sum(len(rows) for rows in first.values()), 32)
+            with self.assertRaises(FileExistsError):
+                write_dataset(root / "first")
+
+    def test_invalid_gold_and_overlap_are_rejected(self) -> None:
+        """Label typos and reused evaluation observations fail loudly."""
+        records = make_records(count=2, seed=9)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            validate_splits({"train": records[:1], "test": records[:1]})
+        invalid = copy.deepcopy(records)
+        invalid[0]["answers"]["verdict"] = "unknown"
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            validate_splits({"train": invalid})
+        invalid = copy.deepcopy(records)
+        invalid[0]["state"]["source_ip"] = "8.8.8.8"
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            validate_splits({"train": invalid})
+
+    def test_generated_prose_requires_reserved_identifiers(self) -> None:
+        """Optional prose cannot add routable IPs or real-looking emails."""
+        validate_summary("Contact user@example.com about host 192.0.2.4.")
+        for text in ("Contact user@company.com", "Connect to 8.8.8.8", "nvapi-" + "a" * 30):
+            with self.subTest(text=text), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                validate_summary(text)
+
+    def test_reporting_keeps_stages_and_checks_counts(self) -> None:
+        """Retain negative changes and reject reports with unequal counts."""
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp:
+            root = Path(temp)
+            for stage, accuracy in (("base", 0.7), ("sft", 0.6)):
+                directory = root / stage
+                directory.mkdir()
+                overall = dict(records=8, n=40, accuracy=accuracy, exact_match=0.5, nll=0.8, brier=0.4, reward=0.3)
+                (directory / "metrics_test.json").write_text(json.dumps({"overall": overall}))
+            rows = summarize_run(root)
+            self.assertLess(rows[1]["accuracy"], rows[0]["accuracy"])
+            path = root / "sft/metrics_test.json"
+            summary = json.loads(path.read_text())
+            summary["overall"]["records"] = 7
+            path.write_text(json.dumps(summary))
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                summarize_run(root)
+

+    unittest.main()
